title: The Number Without a Partner

concept.title: Counting shows who is alone
body: Here every number appears **twice** except one that appears once. Count the numbers in a map and look for the entry with count 1. A cleverer solution exists with bit operations (xor), but counting works for every similar question, for example "the number that appears three times less than the others".
Another way is to keep a **set** and toggle each number: add it if absent, remove it if present. After one pass the set contains only the number without a partner.

statement: A list has an odd number `n` of integers. Every value occurs exactly twice, except one value that occurs exactly once. Print that value.
outputFormat: Print the value that occurs once.
hints: Count how often each value occurs.
Or toggle numbers in a set: add when absent, remove when present.

explanation: Toggling each number in a set leaves exactly the number that appears an odd number of times, the one without a partner.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

alone = set()
for x in a:
    if x in alone:
        alone.remove(x)
    else:
        alone.add(x)
print(next(iter(alone)))
